findings.where: Nav bar, the "Destinations" link (inline on desktop, and in the Menu panel on phone)
findings.fault: The link goes to #destinations, a spot on this same page. This page has no destinations section, so a click does nothing or barely moves the page. It is the only nav link that leads away from this page, so a reader who now trusts the ranking has no working way through to the hostels it ranks.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker. After reading how hostels are ranked, they want to look at the ranked hostels. They tap Destinations and nothing happens, which reads as a broken site on the very page meant to earn their trust.

findings.where: Nav bar wordmark link ("MantaHostels home"), and the footer links Privacy, Terms and Report content
findings.fault: Each of these is a real link, styled as one, but parts.txt shows it leads back to this same page. The home link doesn't go home. Privacy and Terms don't open any policy. Report content gives no way to report anything. A visitor clicking any of them just reloads the page.
findings.who_objects: A careful visitor checking a site they haven't used before, and a hostel owner who wants to flag a review. Privacy, Terms and a reporting route are what such a visitor clicks to test whether a pre-launch site is real. Links that go nowhere undercut a page whose whole job is to be trusted, and leave the owner with no way to report.

findings.fault: The footer wordmark looks like the header's, which is a link, and its turquoise half looks like link colour. But it is static, so a click does nothing. The same mark means "go home" at the top of the page and nothing at the bottom.
findings.who_objects: A visitor at the end of the page who clicks the footer logo to go home, as most sites allow. They get no response and have to scroll back up to the nav.
